strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with quantitative SVD analysis demonstrating 22.9% of features explain 99% of channel variance, justifying efficiency optimization

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple VAE decoders (Wan, LTX-Video), datasets, metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FPS), and hardware platforms (consumer/edge), with strong empirical results: ~6× speedup maintaining 96.9% reconstruction quality
Practical plug-and-play design seamlessly integrating into existing generation pipelines without modification, demonstrating 27-36% end-to-end speedup on Self-Forcing and FastVideo pipelines
Thorough ablation studies systematically validating design choices: pruning methods (Table 3), training strategies (Table 5), pruning ratios, and initialization approaches
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation specifications, multiple benchmark comparisons, promised code release, and clear mathematical formulations
Generalization across diverse VAE decoder architectures (Wan, LTX-Video, Hunyuan, CogVideoX) suggesting broad applicability beyond specific designs
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: channel pruning via R² coefficient, operator replacement via 2D convolutions, and feature distillation are well-established techniques; contribution is primarily in application rather than methodology

Latent distribution preservation claim inadequately supported: relies solely on visual evidence (Figure 10) without quantitative distribution divergence metrics (KL divergence, Wasserstein distance); visualization overlap alone insufficient for core claim

Incomplete justification of critical design choices: loss coefficients (σ₁=10, σ₂=2, σ₃=1, σ₄=5) lack principled justification; three-phase training complexity not compared against simpler alternatives; pruning ratio selection (12.5-25%) appears arbitrary

Limited failure case analysis: Section B.9 acknowledges issues with high-frequency details and temporal dynamics but provides only qualitative examples without systematic characterization of problematic content types or underlying causes

Missing comparisons with alternative efficiency techniques: no evaluation against quantization-aware training, alternative distillation variants, or other pruning strategies; LightVAE quality degradation unexplained
Statistical rigor concerns: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple runs with variance estimation; reported metric differences sometimes marginal without uncertainty quantification

Evaluation scope limitations: primary experiments at 480p, high-resolution results relegated to appendix, limited video content diversity, focus on decoder efficiency while encoder often dominates pipeline costs

Presentation and clarity issues: 9-page appendix indicates organizational problems; Section 3.1 channel pruning methodology unclear; 'independence-aware' framing potentially misleading given standard R² implementation; mathematical notation in Equation 1 could be clearer

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, temporal consistency) and datasets
Substantial speedup (6× or more) while maintaining meaningful reconstruction quality (96.9% fidelity)
Thorough ablation studies examining pruning methods, ratios, initialization strategies, and training approaches
Demonstrates generalization across multiple video generation pipelines (Wan 2.1, LTX-Video, Self-Forcing-Wan)
Well-motivated problem addressing a real bottleneck in video generation systems
Detailed implementation details and supplementary analysis in appendices
weaknesses: Limited novelty: combines standard techniques (channel pruning, operator substitution, knowledge distillation) without fundamental innovation

Weak theoretical justification: the R² coefficient used for pruning decisions doesn't directly measure reconstruction quality; 'independence-aware' selection is just standard linear independence checking
Hyperparameter choices lack principled justification (e.g., loss weights σ₁=10, σ₂=2, σ₃=1, σ₄=5; three-phase training design)
No statistical significance testing or error bars reported despite video quality metrics having inherent variance
Misleading claims: Figure 10 shows visible latent distribution misalignment yet claims 'perfect overlap'
Incomplete failure case analysis: Section B.9 acknowledges limitations (dense objects, high-frequency details) but offers no solutions or deeper investigation
Missing comparisons: no evaluation against other optimization approaches (quantization, mixed-precision training, other pruning methods)
Reproducibility concerns: code not available for review, many design choices unexplained

strengths: Identifies genuine and well-characterized bottlenecks in VAE decoders through thorough analysis (channel redundancy and CausalConv3D computation overhead) with empirical evidence
Demonstrates strong practical results with ~6x VAE decoder speedup while maintaining 96.9% reconstruction quality, and ~0.36x end-to-end pipeline acceleration
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple VAE decoders, diverse metrics, extensive ablation studies, and generalization tests across different resolutions and datasets
Thoughtfully designed three-pronged solution that directly addresses identified bottlenecks, with stage-wise operator optimization appropriately tailored to layer-specific characteristics
Plug-and-play compatibility demonstrated across different generation pipelines (Self-Forcing-Wan 1.3B, FastVideo-Wan 1.3B) with only ~0.27% quality degradation in end-to-end generation
Strong reproducibility practices with detailed implementation details, clear hyperparameters, multiple evaluation settings, and promised code release
Honest treatment of limitations and failure cases, acknowledging trade-offs between efficiency and fine-grained reconstruction capability
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: channel pruning, operator replacement, and distillation training are all well-established techniques; the contribution is primarily their application and combination rather than methodological innovation

Weak theoretical justification for design choices: SVD analysis demonstrates redundancy but limited explanation for why independence-aware pruning is optimal; no principled rationale for three-phase training framework versus alternatives

Generalization concerns: primary evaluation on 480p; scalability to 1080p/4K unclear; limited testing on diverse VAE architectures beyond Wan/LTX-Video; Transformer-based VAEs mentioned but not thoroughly evaluated

Evaluation fairness issues: Flash-VAED uses comprehensive three-phase training while baselines may not employ equivalent strategies; training time costs not reported; comparison against Turbo-VAED appears somewhat unbalanced
Incomplete guidance for practitioners: while failure modes identified in Section B.9, limited principled methods provided for parameter selection when method fails or for content-specific adaptation
Sparse methodological comparisons: limited exploration of other pruning strategies beyond random and L1-norm; other distillation-based acceleration approaches not extensively compared
Critical results relegated to appendices (e.g., Figure 15 scalability analysis) reducing prominence of important findings; Impact Statement section underdeveloped
